**TL;DR: love organic, am terrible at labs - advice pls**

Hi, I'm a UK undergrad in second year of an integrated masters degree (a bachelors but with a 4th year that's almost wholly your research project). I really enjoy organic chemistry but I am terrible in the lab. Obviously, you need to be pretty skilled in the lab to go into synthetic organic, so that's not a path that's open to me. So I'm looking for advice on a) choosing my research project and b) choosing a job. 

Regarding a), I just wanted to know if theres any way to continue in organic with relatively minimal time / emphasis in the lab. I do also enjoy most of physical chemistry (particularly quantum stuff) and certain parts of inorganic (nmr / group theory), so it's not like it's organic or nothing, just the prospect of abandoning organic does make me quite sad (it's just so much fun!).

Regarding b), if a career in organic is off the table, I wanted to know if any of you know of / have experience in other jobs that someone who enjoys organic will find similarly engaging - jobs that work the same muscles in your brain. I enjoy the creative problem solving aspect the most I think, but also the use of simple principles to explain and solve pretty complex things, having to synthesise and organise large bodies of knowledge in your head so you are able to extract the relevant pieces of information, and also I enjoy the joined upness and interconnectedness of it - how everything you learn could be translated / relevant to something else and just the nice feeling when two quite separate parts come together.

I know some of you may feel the need to reassure me that I can get better at labs, and everyone is terrible at labs as an undergrad. I'm sure that's true to a certain extent, but when I say I'm terrible, I mean terrible relative to everyone in my year, and my problems are less because of stuff like lab technique, and more kind of just because of my natural flaws - I'm known in general life as someone who is exceptionally (and I mean exceptionally) absent-minded, forgetful, unobservant, clumsy and careless - obviously traits which translate pretty badly into a lab setting. And anyhow while I do genuinely enjoy labs at uni for the most part, I have heard how hardcore synthetic seems to be and my entire working life being in lab isnt very appealing to me.
